notes: Phase 1 draft. Positions are copied from the current procedural code (world.js / gear.js). 'fit' tells the asset manager how to scale a model from its bounding box, so no hand-computed scale factors are needed. Units: metres, radians, three.js Y-up. Phase 2 adds env, rock materials, sea boulders, and pines. Phase 4 reuses — rough_wood: phase 3 material: createAnimalCase base, clone tinted 0x8a6a56, applyWorldUv(base, 0.5) | rock_cliff: phase 2: gallery shell boxes (dark 0x14110e), clone tinted 0x4a423a, applyWorldUv(box, 2.42) | rock_floor: phase 2: gallery floor boxes (0x1a1612) tinted 0x5a5048 with tile 2.0; gear.js puzzle plinth untinted with tile 2.0

crate.orientation: long axis (+Z) along the pile's row direction; derive w/d (and userData.hx/hz/stackSpan) from the scaled model bbox
crate.collider: keep the existing BoxGeometry mesh as the raycast/chop/stand proxy with material.visible = false, sized to the scaled model bbox

hatchet.keep: userData.blade (move this invisible marker to the model's blade centre), userData.grip, holdPose()

rockMaterials.usedBy: world.js createCliff() rock boxes (mass, slab, beach, pad, ladder course/rung, jamb, brow, haunch) and createWorld() addRock()/wallMat
rockMaterials.rule: rock_floor for beach, pad, ladder courses and rungs; rock_cliff for everything else. Rewrite each box's UVs in world space (applyWorldUv(mesh, tileM)) after the mesh is positioned.

seaRocks.stonesNote: [k, dx, dz, salt]: the main stone and the two biggest satellites of addSeaOutcrop()'s 5 stones.
seaRocks.rule: s = 2*scale*k / max(nativeSize.x, nativeSize.z); top = k === 1 ? WATER_Y + scale*0.95 : WATER_Y + scale*k*0.55; position (x + dx*scale, top - bboxMax.y*s, z + dz*scale); rotation.y = hash01(seed + salt + 3) * 6.2. Then raycast straight down at each outcrop (x, z) to get the real perch height for createBirds().

forest.rule: keep scatter() unchanged but tag each spot with its band (0 = the three 3.5 m scatters, 1 = the three 7.2 m scatters, 2 = the three 15 m scatters). band 0: hash01(x*5.3 + z*2.9) < 0.5 ? pine_a : pine_b; band 1: pine_b; band 2: pine_far. One InstancedMesh per (variant, part) = 5 InstancedMeshes. Matrix: position (x, 0, z), rotation.y = spot.spin, uniform scale spot.h / bboxMax.y.

sky_backdrop.encoding: KTX2 UASTC + zstd, sRGB, no mipmaps, stored bottom-up (KTX2 textures cannot flipY)
sky_backdrop.use: map of the existing sky sphere (SphereGeometry r=120) after geometry.scale(-1,1,1).rotateY(Math.PI), side FrontSide, wrapS RepeatWrapping, Linear filters, toneMapped stays true
sky_backdrop.note: Pre-rotated so the HDRI moon sits at the azimuth of the old procedural moon mesh (-22, 9, 1); no rotation needed in code.

sky_env.use: HDRLoader (three r180; RGBELoader is deprecated) with HalfFloatType -> mapping EquirectangularReflectionMapping -> PMREMGenerator.fromEquirectangular() -> scene.environment; dispose the source texture afterwards
sky_env.note: Moon disc clamped out (54% of the HDRI's energy; the key DirectionalLight already plays the moon) and normalised to mean radiance 0.541 = main.js envScene sphere 0xb7c4d0, so scene.environmentIntensity 1 gives about today's ambient level.

water_normal.encoding: KTX2 UASTC + zstd, linear (no sRGB), 10 mip levels, normals re-normalised
water_normal.use: tangent-space detail normals for src/water.js: RepeatWrapping, sampled twice (3.7 m and 11.3 m tiles)
